prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCCN1C[C@@H](O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)[C@H](CC(N)=O)NC(=O)c1ccc2ccccc2n1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL243

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibitory potency against HIV-1 protease
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibitory activity against purified HIV-1 protease (BH10) at a pH of 4.7 and a final enzyme concentration of 0.45-1.1 nM
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.55, "error_class": "buffer_conditions", "reason": "Assay B explicitly specifies a pH of 4.7, which is unusually low for HIV-1 protease assays (typically pH 5.5–6.0), and this non-standard pH condition can significantly shift IC50 values compared to a standard assay, making the two measurements likely to differ by more than 1.0 log unit."}

parsed.reason: Assay B explicitly specifies a pH of 4.7, which is unusually low for HIV-1 protease assays (typically pH 5.5–6.0), and this non-standard pH condition can significantly shift IC50 values compared to a standard assay, making the two measurements likely to differ by more than 1.0 log unit.
